answer.rationale: Write-path p99 at 5x with settlement at daily peak and heavy writes looks like saturation; b3 is the closest prior lesson (headroom kept queues flat through a surge) and adding capacity does not drop customer writes. Cause is not identified: a release shipped 2h ago and latency has climbed for 90m, so b1 (rollback cleared a post-release checkout error spike) remains a live alternative. Not choosing rollback yet because the current symptom is latency under peak writes, not an error spike, and a write-path rollback mid-settlement could lose or disrupt customer writes. Circuit breakers would fail writes; read-replica routing and regional failover are weaker matches (no report-load or regional signal). Verifying b3 before commit because that case provisioned headroom before the peak—unclear it applies as a mid-peak add. Scale is a meaningful but not fleet-wide capacity add so the single window can actually absorb load without assuming the bottleneck. Settlement value is at risk if writes are shed or the wrong lever is used.
